evidence: LOW CONFIDENCE. B comes from the two tests side by side. BB4 is the cure-class leg of 29-4 with an earlier date and a stricter bar, so once BB4 fires the major needs only its other leg: a pembrolizumab copy on sale in the US or EU by Nov 30, 2029. B is the odds of that leg, 75 on the graph's own figure (one_number_rule of 29-4). History brackets it at about 60 to 80. Of the 3 cancer antibodies with US copies, Mvasi (Avastin) and Kanjinti (Herceptin) both launched in Jul 2019, as the main US patents ran out (Jul 2019 and Jun 2019 on Roche's stated dates), and Truxima (Rituxan) launched in Nov 2019 under a settlement, a year after its approval: 3 of 3 gives 80 and 2 of 3 gives 60 by the rule of succession. Against that, a study of 32 US biosimilars found the median launch 2.3 to 2.5 years after the primary patent expired, and Merck's 10-K lists the US compound patent to 2028 with two more of the same family to 2029 and EU cover to 2031, so only the US route can meet the date. FDA accepted the first copy filing (Formycon and Zydus, FYB206) in Oct 2026, decision expected Q3 2027. Ceiling: with B = 100 the formula gives 0.533, so the current 0.8 cannot hold (it drives 29-4 to 99 with the copies leg still open). Second form: C = 0.75 x (59 - 25) / (100 - 25) = 34, so B - C = 0.41; the gap is a level issue: 29-4 sits at 60 on a 'lower leg' rule while the two legs multiplied give about 44.
